prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2019 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core vision
- Build a fair, free and open society, prioritising liberty, equality, community and wellbeing. Put people and planet first; disperse power; champion diversity and creativity.

Stop Brexit
- If winning a majority on a Stop Brexit platform: revoke Article 50 and remain in the EU. Otherwise, back a People’s Vote with the option to remain.
- Use a £50bn “Remain Bonus” from stronger growth to invest in schools, public services and tackling inequality.
- Protect freedom of movement and extend full voting rights to EU citizens resident 5+ years.

Economy and tax
- Invest £130bn in infrastructure (transport, energy, schools, hospitals, housing) plus a £50bn Regional Rebalancing Programme and a £5bn Green Investment Bank.
- Make the UK innovation-led: raise R&D to 3% of GDP; expand Catapult centres; boost regional clusters; support creative industries.
- Fair taxes: restore Corporation Tax to 20%; replace Business Rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy; tackle multinational tax avoidance; tax capital gains like income.

Work, skills and business
- Create a £10,000 Skills Wallet for every adult (ages 25/40/55) and broaden the apprenticeship levy into a wider Skills & Training Levy.
- Modernise rights for the gig economy (new “dependent contractor” status; flexible working from day one; fairer zero-hours rules).
- Support entrepreneurs with a start-up allowance, prompt payment enforcement and expanded British Business Bank.

Education and childcare
- Free, high-quality childcare from 9 months for working parents; 35 hours/week for 2–4-year‑olds.
- Reverse school cuts; hire 20,000 teachers; fix buildings.
- Replace SATs and league tables; scrap Ofsted for a broader inspectorate; protect arts; introduce a “curriculum for life.”
- Extend free school meals and breakfast clubs; embed mental health support in schools.
- FE: +£1bn; restore maintenance grants; Student Mental Health Charter.

Climate, nature and transport
- Net zero by 2045; 80% renewable electricity by 2030; ban fracking.
- Ten‑year programme to insulate homes; zero‑carbon new buildings by 2021; end fuel poverty by 2025.
- Plant 60m trees/year; a Zero‑Waste & Resource Efficiency Act; stronger protections for nature and oceans.
- Transport: Clean Air Act; all new cars/vans electric by 2030; electrify rail by 2035; freeze commuter fares for a parliament; £4.5bn to restore bus routes; 10% of transport budget for walking/cycling; oppose airport expansion.

Health and social care
- Add 1p to Income Tax to raise £7bn/year for the NHS and social care; £10bn capital for modern facilities.
- Mental health parity: new waiting time standards; 24/7 crisis care in all hospitals; expand talking therapies; perinatal support; end police cells for crises.

A fair society
- Reform Universal Credit (five-week wait cut to five days; end two‑child limit and benefit cap; boost work allowances); legal right to food.
- Build 300,000 homes/year, including 100,000 for social rent; zero‑carbon standards; end rough sleeping within five years.
- Public health: regulated cannabis market; obesity strategy; air quality right; PrEP access; minimum unit pricing for alcohol.

Rights, equality and immigration
- Defend the Human Rights Act and ECHR; halt police facial recognition; Lovelace Code on AI/data.
- Tackle hate crime; reform Gender Recognition Act; X‑gender passports; British Sign Language Act; end period poverty.
- Scrap the hostile environment; end indefinite detention (28‑day limit); right to work for asylum seekers after 3 months; welcome refugees (including 10,000 unaccompanied children over 10 years).

Political reform and devolution
- Proportional representation (STV); votes at 16; reform House of Lords; stronger rules on money, media and online ads.
- A written federal constitution; significant devolution of powers and funding to nations, regions and communities.

Global role and defence
- Lead international cooperation via EU, UN, NATO; retain 0.7% aid; stricter arms controls (suspend sales to Saudi Arabia); Magnitsky sanctions.
- Defence at 2% of GDP; cyber readiness; maintain a reduced, credible nuclear deterrent; recognise Palestine; support Hong Kong BN(O) holders.
